title: Tanzu Valkey - Sentinel HA Overview
description: Valkey Sentinel (primary/replica) operations dashboard for Tanzu for Valkey on Kubernetes

list.name: Primary changed
list.expr: count by (pod) ({__name__="${prefix}_instance_info", namespace="$namespace", role="master"}) unless count by (pod) ({__name__="${prefix}_instance_info", namespace="$namespace", role="master"} offset 1m)

list.name: prefix
list.label: Metric prefix
list.description: Exporter metric prefix. Tanzu Valkey 3.5.1 (exporter v1.82.0) uses redis; pick valkey for builds that use that prefix.

panels.title: Data pods up
panels.description: Number of Valkey data pods the exporter can reach.

panels.title: Current primary (writer)
panels.description: Pod currently reporting role=master.

targets.expr: sum(rate({__name__="${prefix}_keyspace_hits_total", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum(rate({__name__="${prefix}_keyspace_hits_total", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum(rate({__name__="${prefix}_keyspace_misses_total", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Role and placement (pod -> role -> Kubernetes node)
panels.description: Which pod is the writer, which are replicas, and the worker node each one runs on. Version is valkey_version (INFO server). redis_version is always 7.2.4, a Redis-compatibility value, so it isn't shown.

targets.expr: max by (pod, role, node, valkey_version) ({__name__="${prefix}_instance_info", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})

panels.title: Primary over time (failover history)
panels.description: PRIMARY marks the pod that held the writer role at each point in time. A colour change = failover.

targets.expr: max by (pod) ({__name__="${prefix}_instance_info", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod", role="master"}) or (max by (pod) ({__name__="${prefix}_instance_info", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod", role="slave"}) * 0)

panels.title: Valkey process CPU (cores)
panels.description: used_cpu_sys + used_cpu_user from INFO. Valkey executes commands on one main thread: ~1.0 core means saturated.

targets.expr: rate({__name__="${prefix}_cpu_sys_seconds_total", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]) + on (namespace, pod) rate({__name__="${prefix}_cpu_user_seconds_total", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])

panels.title: Container CPU vs limit (cores)
panels.description: cAdvisor view of every container in the pod (valkey, exporter, sidecars).

targets.expr: sum by (pod, container) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container!="", container!="POD"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: CPU throttling
panels.description: Share of CFS periods throttled. Sustained throttling adds latency: raise the CPU limit.

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container!=""}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_periods_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container!=""}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Memory used vs maxmemory
panels.description: used_memory (dataset + overhead), used_memory_rss (as seen by the OS) and maxmemory. maxmemory=0 means unlimited: the container limit becomes the real ceiling (OOMKill).

panels.title: Fragmentation ratio (rss / used)
panels.description: < 1.0 = swapping (bad). 1.0-1.5 = healthy. > 1.5 = fragmented: consider activedefrag. Ignore on near-empty instances.

panels.title: Container memory vs limit
panels.description: If the working set reaches the limit the kubelet OOMKills the container.

panels.title: Evicted / expired keys per second
panels.description: Evictions mean maxmemory was hit and the eviction policy is deleting data.

panels.title: Memory used by role
panels.description: Replicas should track the primary closely; a gap means a replica is behind or resyncing.

targets.expr: sum by (role) ({__name__="${prefix}_memory_used_bytes", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} * on (namespace, pod) group_left (role) {__name__="${prefix}_instance_info", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})

panels.title: Hit rate by pod
panels.description: hits / (hits + misses) for read commands.

targets.expr: rate({__name__="${prefix}_keyspace_hits_total", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]) / on (namespace, pod) (rate({__name__="${prefix}_keyspace_hits_total", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]) + on (namespace, pod) rate({__name__="${prefix}_keyspace_misses_total", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Network throughput
panels.description: Client + replication traffic. Output shown as negative. The primary's output includes the replication stream to every replica.

panels.title: New / rejected connections per second
panels.description: A high rate of new connections suggests clients are not pooling. Any rejected connection means maxclients was reached.

panels.title: Replication offset lag (bytes behind primary)
panels.description: Difference between the highest replication offset and each pod's offset. Should hover around 0.

panels.title: Replica lag reported by primary (s)
panels.description: Seconds since each replica last acknowledged the stream (from INFO replication on the primary).

panels.title: Replica link status / connected replicas
panels.description: master_link_up=1 on every replica; connected_slaves on the primary = replica count.

panels.title: Average latency per command (µs)
panels.description: Server-side execution time only (excludes network and queueing).

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (cmd) (rate({__name__="${prefix}_commands_duration_seconds_total", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (cmd) (rate({__name__="${prefix}_commands_total", namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) * 1e6)

panels.title: Slowlog length
panels.description: Commands slower than slowlog-log-slower-than. Inspect with SLOWLOG GET.
